questions.stem: Your father's father is your:

options.explanation: Correct. A relative reached through your father is paternal, and your father's father is two steps up the direct line — your paternal grandfather.
The maternal grandfather is your mother's father. This relative is reached through the father, so the label is paternal.
A paternal uncle is your father's brother — the same generation as your father. Your father's father sits one generation higher.
A father-in-law is the father of your spouse, a relation by marriage. Your father's father is joined to you by blood.

questions.stem: Your mother's brother is your:

options.explanation: A paternal uncle is your father's brother. This relative is reached through the mother, so the label is maternal.
Correct. A brother of your mother is your maternal uncle — in everyday Indian usage, 'mama'.
A brother-in-law is your spouse's brother or your sister's husband, a relation by marriage. Your mother's brother is blood kin.
A cousin is the child of an uncle or aunt — your own generation. Your mother's brother is a generation above you.

questions.sourceRef: Maternal uncle = the mother's brother

questions.stem: Your father's sister is your:

options.explanation: A maternal aunt is your mother's sister ('mausi'). This relative is reached through the father, so she is a paternal aunt.
A sister-in-law is joined by marriage — your spouse's sister or your brother's wife. Your father's sister is blood kin.
Correct. A sister of your father is your paternal aunt — in everyday Indian usage, 'bua'.
A cousin is your own generation. Your father's sister is one generation above you.

questions.sourceRef: Paternal aunt = the father's sister

questions.stem: Your son's wife is your:

options.explanation: A daughter is joined to you by blood. Your son's wife married into the family, so the link is by marriage, not descent.
Correct. Your son's wife is your daughter-in-law — the same generation as your child, female, joined by marriage.
A sister-in-law is your spouse's sister or your brother's wife, in your own generation. Your son's wife is one generation below you.
A niece is your sibling's daughter, joined by blood. Your son's wife is joined by marriage.

questions.sourceRef: Daughter-in-law = the son's wife, a relation by marriage

questions.stem: P is the father of Q, Q is the father of R, and R is the father of S. Counting P's level as the first, how many generations does the line from P down to S span?

options.explanation: Three counts only P, Q and R, or leaves out one level. The direct line runs P, Q, R, S — four levels.
Correct. Each 'father of' step drops one generation: P (1), Q (2), R (3), S (4). Four distinct levels means four generations.
Five would need a fifth person below S. The chain stops at S, the fourth level.
Two levels would be a single parent-child pair. There are three parent-child links here, so four levels.

questions.stem: X is described only as 'the cousin of Y'. What can be said about X's gender?

options.explanation: The word 'cousin' carries no gender in English. Nothing here makes X male.
The word 'cousin' carries no gender. Nothing here makes X female.
Correct. 'Cousin' is a gender-free word, like child, spouse, sibling and in-law. With no other clue, X's gender cannot be fixed.

options.text: X is the same gender as Y
options.explanation: Cousins can be of any gender, unrelated to each other's. The word settles nothing about X's gender.

questions.sourceRef: Cousin is a gender-free word

questions.stem: Which of these relationship words fixes the gender of the person it names?

options.explanation: Correct. 'Daughter' is always female. Words like daughter, son, mother, father, uncle, aunt, husband and wife each fix a gender.
'Child' is gender-free — a child may be a son or a daughter.
'Cousin' is gender-free and settles nothing about gender.
'Spouse' is gender-free — a spouse may be a husband or a wife.

questions.sourceRef: Son, daughter, mother, father and the like fix a gender; child, cousin, spouse do not

questions.stem: M is the child of N, and M is the parent of O. From this alone, is M a father or a mother?

options.explanation: This assumes M is male. 'Child' and 'parent' are both gender-free, so nothing fixes M as a father.
This assumes M is female. Neither 'child' nor 'parent' states M's gender.
Correct. M is described only as a child and a parent, both gender-free words. Whether M is a father or a mother cannot be determined from this alone.
O's presence says nothing about M's gender. A parent of O may be a father or a mother.

questions.sourceRef: Child and parent are gender-free; M's gender is not fixed

questions.topic: Ch 12 · Blood Relations · Two-sided in-law word
questions.stem: R says that S is his brother-in-law. From this statement alone, how exactly is S related to R?

options.text: S is the brother of R's wife
options.explanation: This is one valid reading, but not the only one. 'Brother-in-law' can also mean the husband of R's sister.

options.text: S is the husband of R's sister
options.explanation: This is one valid reading, but not the only one. 'Brother-in-law' can also mean the brother of R's wife.

options.text: Either of these — it cannot be uniquely determined
options.explanation: Correct. 'Brother-in-law' covers two different people: the spouse's brother and the sister's husband. From the word alone, R's exact link to S cannot be settled.

options.text: S is the brother of R
options.explanation: A brother is joined by blood. 'Brother-in-law' names a relation by marriage, not a brother.

questions.sourceRef: Brother-in-law = the spouse's brother OR the sister's husband

questions.stem: Paper 3 gives 1 mark for a correct answer and deducts 0.25 for a wrong one. On four purely blind guesses among four options each, what is the expected net mark?

options.explanation: Correct. On average one of four blind guesses is right (+1) and three are wrong (3 × −0.25 = −0.75), a net of +0.25 across the four attempts.
This ignores the deductions. The three wrong guesses remove 0.75, leaving a net of only 0.25.
The expected value is slightly positive, not zero, because a right answer earns more than a wrong one loses.
This counts only the deductions and forgets the mark earned by the one correct guess.

questions.sourceRef: Blind guessing among four: +1 once, −0.25 three times, net +0.25

questions.topic: Ch 12 · Blood Relations · Value of elimination
questions.stem: In a four-option question, you rule out one option as clearly wrong and then guess among the rest. How often is that guess correct on average?

options.explanation: Correct. Removing one of four options leaves three, so a guess among them is right one time in three — better than the one-in-four of a blind guess.
One in four is the blind rate before any elimination. Ruling out an option improves the odds to one in three.
One in two would need two options ruled out, leaving only two. Here only one option is removed.
Guessing among three real options is often right. Elimination raises the chance of a correct guess, it does not remove it.

readLink.label: Read: Negative marking and when to leave a question, §7 →

questions.sourceRef: Ruling out one of four options gives a one-in-three guess

questions.topic: Ch 12 · Blood Relations · When 'cannot be determined' is right
questions.stem: In a blood-relations question, a gender needed for the exact answer is never stated, and the single-word answer would change depending on it. 'Cannot be determined' is one of the options. What is the best response?

options.explanation: Correct. When the answer genuinely flips with a gender the puzzle never gave you, 'cannot be determined' is the intended answer, included precisely to catch the student who assumes.

options.text: Assume the person is male and answer accordingly
options.explanation: Assuming a gender is exactly the trap. If the answer depends on that assumption, the correct choice is 'cannot be determined'.

options.text: Assume the person is female and answer accordingly
options.explanation: This makes the same unwarranted assumption in the other direction. The puzzle withheld the gender on purpose.
Leaving it blank scores zero when a correct option — 'cannot be determined' — is actually available. Select it and claim the mark.

questions.sourceRef: 'Cannot be determined' is a real answer when an unstated gender changes the result
